name: code_map
description: Get the architectural map of a repository: module communities with their key symbols and files, ranked by size. Prefer this over directory listings or file reads when orienting in an unfamiliar codebase -- the answer is pre-indexed. Scope: always the calling session's own repo -- a member session uses its registered work folder; any other session uses the first MCP client root (roots/list) inside a git repository with an origin remote, as that repository's top level -- the same repository its kb_* tools use -- or the fleet server's working folder when the client offers no roots. Extension for code tools only: when roots are offered and none has an origin remote, the first offered git repository is used (kb_* tools then fail with E-SELF-NO-REMOTE). There is no repo/path scope argument. Fails with E-SELF-NO-WORKFOLDER or E-SELF-NOT-A-REPO when that folder is missing or is not a git repository, E-CODE-INDEX-NOT-READY when it has no usable code index yet (a missing or interrupted index gets a build requested automatically -- retry shortly) or the index is still building (that error's text and structuredContent carry retry_after_ms -- wait that long once, retry once, then fall back; never poll code_status in a loop -- plus retry_will_help and, while an analyze runs, its progress), and E-CODE-INTEL-DISABLED when code intelligence is off (each with a one-line remediation).
